summary: Intermittent throughput collapse and p95 latency spikes for batched inference on dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary: Stratosight is seeing recurring, short-lived collapses in throughput and p95 latency spikes (up to 6-10x baseline) for inference requests routed to their dedicated pool. Impact: customer applications experience 504s and aborted streaming responses for ~30-90s windows multiple times per hour, affecting user-facing search and summarization features. Environment: prod (us-west-2) dedicated pool reserved for Stratosight with mixed-instance nodes and custom autoscaler profile. Timeline: first reported 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC; multiple recurrences observed through 2026-03-10 afternoon and again on 2026-03-11.

Observations: metrics show p95 token latency jumping from ~220ms to >2s, 5xx count increases, and sustained queue growth on gateway. GPU dashboards indicate high SM utilization and rising GPU memory fragmentation during incidents while host CPU remains moderate. Autoscaler logs show several rapid scale-down events in the 5 minutes prior to degraded windows.

Expected behavior: steady throughput within SLA, graceful queueing without intermittent 504s. Workaround requested: immediate mitigation to keep customer service online while we investigate root cause.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send sustained batched requests that target long context lengths (avg 1024 tokens) and bathtub shapes (bursty traffic) to customer's dedicated pool endpoint.
2) Mix model variants in traffic (open-llama-7b-v2 + redwood-mix-medium) and include a subset of high-beam and sampling calls to increase KV cache pressure.
3) Observe p95 latency and request queue depth in serving-console over 5-15 minute windows; reproduce under autoscaler set to min=2, max=6, scaleDownAggressiveness=high (customer config).
logs: 2026-03-10T09:10:22Z gateway: upstream queue depth for pool-stratosight increased to 420 (baseline 38)
2026-03-10T09:11:07Z autoscaler: scaled down node-group-a from 5 -> 3 due to short-term cpu drop (policy: aggressive)

2026-03-10T09:11:34Z serving-runtime: kernel stall detected on GPU gpu-0 (SM busy 98%, active warps stalled)
stack: merge-kernel-1 -> attention-fused -> kv-cache-commit
2026-03-10T09:12:00Z gateway: returned 504 to request id req-7f3b2 (timeout 30s)
comments: Ava Martin (2026-03-10 09:18): Customer reported first outage. Collected traces and requested SRE review. Asked customer to enable debug streaming for next window.

Diego Ramos (2026-03-10 09:35): Initial triage: autoscaler triggered rapid scale-downs before incidents. Hypothesis: aggressive scale-down + mixed heavy batches causing head-of-line blocking and GPU memory churn. Opening investigation with serving-runtime and scheduler teams.

SRE Pager (2026-03-10 10:05): Temporarily pinned pool to 4 nodes and disabled aggressive scale-down for customer pool. Noted immediate partial improvement but residual latency spikes persisted during co-tenant high memory jobs.
Customer (Stratosight Ops) (2026-03-10 10:28): Confirmed reduced 504s after pin, but still seeing spikes tied to specific time windows (every ~20-40 minutes). Provided logs of in-app batch storms.

Serving-runtime Eng (2026-03-11 14:12): Observed KV cache pressure and elevated GPU memory fragmentation when mixing model variants. Reproduced locally by replaying customer traffic; profiling attached to PR.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Autoscaler misconfiguration allowed scale-down during transient load dips, producing insufficient GPU capacity when burst arrived. Evidence: autoscaler events precede incident windows and pool size shrank 1-2 nodes within 2-3 minutes.

Hypothesis 2: Noisy neighbor from co-tenant batch jobs pinned to same nodes causing GPU memory fragmentation and kernel stalls. Evidence: during incidents non-customer pods observed with large memory allocations and elevated cudaMalloc times.

Hypothesis 3: Scheduler lacked affinity rules for model memory class; heavy and light models co-located increasing eviction/GC cycles in serving-runtime. Reproduced by mixing open-llama-7b-v2 and redwood-mix-medium in same node set — p95 increases and SM stalls observed.

Profiling: nvprof traces show long kernel tail on fused attention kernel when fragmentation rises. GPU_util high but effective throughput low. Serving-runtime logs show repeated KV cache invalidations leading to re-computation overhead.

Temporary mitigations tried: pinned node count to fixed level, increased per-pool node isolation, and temporarily routed heavy-batch traffic to fallback smaller model. Pin reduced 504s but did not eliminate transient spikes during simultaneous co-tenant jobs.
resolution_notes: Mitigation applied (2026-03-11 16:30): Autoscaler policy for customer pool modified to set min=4, max=8, scaleDownAggressiveness=low and add cooldown 300s. Nodes with heavy-memory pods drained from mixed pools and moved to dedicated slot-pools.
Routing change (2026-03-11 18:00): Implemented short-term routing rule to avoid co-scheduling open-llama-7b-v2 with redwood-mix-medium on same GPU nodes for Stratosight traffic.
Hotfix (2026-03-12 02:10): Serving-runtime PR merged to reduce KV cache invalidation frequency for mixed model workloads (PR #4212). This reduced observed re-compute spikes in replay tests.
Customer impact: Incident windows frequency dropped to near zero and p95 returned to within SLA for 48h post-mitigation. Customer confirmed production stability on 2026-03-12.

Long-term actions: scheduler will receive an enhancement to consider model memory class and sequence-length distribution when placing pods; autoscaler UX will include safeguards against aggressive scale-down on dedicated pools. Follow-up tickets created: INT-4127 (scheduler affinity), SUP-82701 (autoscaler UX for dedicated).
